Nina (Support): Hey team — FinServX (prod) hit a cascade: model/tool-call failures + intermittent 401s. Customer reports two things: 
1) function call is rejected with \"invalid_tool_arguments: expected accounts as array<string>, got string\"
2) model returned \"malformed JSON\" on some retries. They retried automatically and saw a billing spike. Repro + logs below.

Nina (Support): Repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
  -d '{
    \"model\": \"redwood-alpha-1\",
    \"messages\": [{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Upsert accounts\"}],
    \"json_mode\": true,
    \"tool_call\": {
      \"name\": \"upsert_accounts\",
      \"arguments\": {
        \"accounts\": \"[\\\"acct_1\\\",\\\"acct_2\\\"]\",    // <-- stringified array (BAD)
        \"source\": \"stripe\"
      }
    }
  }'
```

Nina (Support): Customer logs (stack-snips):
```
error_id=req_0a1b2c3d status=400 error=invalid_tool_arguments details=\"accounts: expected array<string>, got string\"
warning: auth=401 request_id=req_0a1b2c3d retry=1
info: latency_ms=3900 model_response=partial_malformed_json
```

Tom (SRE): Thanks. Can you confirm request_id and customer org id? Any sample of the exact model output that triggered \"malformed JSON\"?

Nina (Support): req_0a1b2c3d, org=finservx-prod. Pasting the truncated model response we stored: 
```
{\"tool_call\": {\"name\":\"upsert_accounts\", \"arguments\": \"{\\\"accounts\\\": \"[\\\\\\\"acct_1\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"acct_2\\\\\\\"]\"}\"}}

# parser error: unexpected token '\"' at position 21
```

Maya (Engine): This looks like double-encoding: the SDK or client is stringifying the nested array, so the model/runtime sees a string instead of an array. That explains the invalid_tool_arguments. The \"malformed JSON\" can come from the model attempting to emit structured output and hitting the already-stringified value.

Raj (Platform): Two quick mitigation paths:
- short-term: set permissive_arg_coercion=true on the route to accept stringified arrays and coerce them to arrays (if safe).
- mid-term: add a runtime sanitizer that detects JSON-encoded strings for fields declared as arrays and coerce when unambiguous.

Raj (Platform): Example of short-term override (support can instruct customer):
```json
{ \"permissive_arg_coercion\": true }
```
(Note: feature gated, requires support flag on tenant)

Maya (Engine): Also found a pattern in SDK v0.9 where nested arrays are JSON.stringified by default when using convenience helpers. Patch idea: detect string that matches JSON array regex ^\\s*\[.*\]\\s*$ and attempt JSON.parse if declared schema expects array<string>. I'll draft a runtime-safe coercion that logs when it happens.

Maya (Engine): Minimal fix customer can apply immediately: pass arrays directly. Node example: 
```js
// BAD: stringified
client.call({tool_call: {name: 'upsert_accounts', arguments: {accounts: JSON.stringify(['acct_1','acct_2'])}}})
// GOOD: pass array
client.call({tool_call: {name: 'upsert_accounts', arguments: {accounts: ['acct_1','acct_2']}}})
```

Alejandro (FinOps): FYI — we saw a billing spike for org finservx-prod during the incident window. Retries x3 on failure drove token usage up ~4.2x. Customer asking for short-term credit; support, please flag billing.

Nina (Support): Marking P1 for triage. Rafael (CS lead) asked to prioritize refund review and safety fix. Will request permissive_arg_coercion enable while engineering ships patch.

Maya (Engine): I'll open PR #4872 for runtime coercion + logging. Will add a unit that detects stringified arrays/objects when schema expects list/object. Canary suggestion: route=canary(5%) first.

Tom (SRE): Also saw the intermittent 401s — token refresh errors from the customer's upstream auth provider. Those retries overlapped with invalid args and made the behaviour noisy. Recommend we advise the customer to exponential-backoff for 401s and reduce aggressive retry count for now.

Nina (Support): Action items: 1) Support: ask customer to send arrays (one-off customer note) and open billing credit request. 2) Platform: enable permissive_arg_coercion for finservx-prod (temporary). 3) Engine: PR for coercion + canary. 4) SRE: confirm no other tenants impacted by 401 bursts.

Maya (Engine): I'll schedule the canary after PR lands. Planning window: patch + CI today, canary 5% tomorrow 03:00 UTC, full rollout after 24h validation.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: PR #4872 -> canary 5% at 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC.

Nina (Support): I'll follow up with customer with repro notes and temporary config. Updating ticket FIN-9874.

Alejandro (FinOps): I'll produce the billing impact summary and suggested credit amount, posting in the ticket in 2h.

Maya (Engine): If anyone has additional sample traces (esp. model payload that shows stringified nested json), drop them here and I'll add to the test matrix.

Nina (Support): Will add request logs from finservx-prod (sanitized) to the ticket. Thanks all.
